Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

establish verb

set up, found

also set up, found a school, found a city, institute

classical

Quint. 1.8.5: optimē īnstitūtum est, ut ab Homērō atque Vergiliō lēctiō inciperet
Liv. 5.27.2: cum in pāce īnstituisset puerōs ante urbem lūsūs exercendīque causā prōdūcere

īnstituō, īnstituere, īnstituī, īnstitūtum

verb, third conjugation; with an accusative, or an infinitive (to make a practice of doing)

set up, establish (a custom, a practice, a school)

Lewis & Short: “to set up, erect, plant, establish, arrange”; an established practice is īnstitūtum (see practice, custom). Also to train or educate a child (Traupman 29). That something is an established fact is cōnstat (Liv. 3.26.9: id quod cōnstat).

Examples

  • optimē īnstitūtum est, ut ab Homērō atque Vergiliō lēctiō inciperet

    It is an excellent established custom that reading should begin with Homer and Vergil.Quint. 1.8.5

  • tantae mōlis erat Rōmānam condere gentem

    So great a task it was to found the Roman people.Verg. A. 1.33

  • tempora dīgereret cum conditor urbis, in annō cōnstituit mēnsēs quīnque bis esse suō

    When the founder of the city was setting the calendar in order, he established that his year should have twice five months.Ov. F. 1.27–28

Other words

  • cōnstituō, cōnstituere, cōnstituī, cōnstitūtum — establish, settle, fix (a state, laws, a date)

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ov. F. 1.27–28: in annō cōnstituit mēnsēs quīnque bis esse suō

  • condō, condere, condidī, conditum — found (a city, a people)

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.33: tantae mōlis erat Rōmānam condere gentem

    See also create.

See also create, practice, introduce.
